messages.text: 'A joke' - Hussain fumes as day three at Lord's abandoned amid sunshine

metadata.summary: A seething Nasser Hussain said the umpires' decision to abandon play late on day three of the second Test between England and Pakistan was "a joke".
metadata.content: England vs Pakistan: Nasser Hussain fumes as day three of second Test at Lord's abandoned during sunshine | Cricket News | Sky Sports Skip to content England vs Pakistan: Nasser Hussain fumes as day three of second Test at Lord's abandoned during sunshine Just 24.5 overs possible on Saturday of second Test due to bad light and rain; stumps called at 6.30pm despite sun shining; Dan Lawrence's sixth Test fifty, notched from 64 balls, features stunning six; watch day four from 10.15am, Sunday, Sky Sports Cricket Nasser Hussain Cricket expert and columnist Saturday 29 August 2026 19:35, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Nasser Hussain questioned the umpires' decision to end play on day three of the second Test between England and Pakistan with the sun shining at the time A seething Nasser Hussain said the umpires' decision to abandon play late on day three of the second Test between England and Pakistan was "a joke". Just 24.5 overs were possible on a gloomy Saturday due to rain and bad light, during which time England moved from their overnight 81-3 to 177-7 for a lead of 357 as they look to wrap up a series win. There looked to be a chance of more cricket when the sun began to shine late in the evening, only for the day to be officially called off just after 6.30pm local time, prompting heavy booing from spectators. messages.text: Iraola fumes at electronic board issue which delayed Liverpool subs before Forest pen

metadata.summary: Andoni Iraola said Nottingham Forest's penalty in the 2-2 draw at Anfield on Saturday would not have occurred if the fourth official's electronic board was working correctly.
metadata.content: Liverpool: Andoni Iraola says fourth official's electronic board issue delayed subs ahead of Nottingham Forest being awarded penalty | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to content Liverpool: Andoni Iraola says fourth official's electronic board issue delayed subs ahead of Nottingham Forest being awarded penalty Liverpool were frustrated at being unable to make a triple substitution before Nottingham Forest were awarded a penalty on Saturday, with an electronic board issue meaning they missed three opportunities to make the change in the eventual 2-2 draw Peter Smith Senior Football Journalist @psmithXI Saturday 29 August 2026 17:58, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola was frustrated at being unable to make substitutions prior to Nottingham Forest's penalty award Andoni Iraola said Nottingham Forest's penalty in the 2-2 draw at Anfield on Saturday would not have occurred if the fourth official's electronic board was working correctly. Forest took the lead for the second time in the match on 70 minutes, when Morgan Gibbs-White converted from the spot after Neco Williams had been fouled by Alisson. At that point, Liverpool had been trying to make a triple substitution for over two minutes - during which time the ball had gone out of play on three occasions.
